what: MPLX owns midstream energy infrastructure: crude and refined product pipelines, marine vessels, terminals and natural gas gathering and processing plants. It is controlled by Marathon Petroleum, which is also its largest customer.
customers: Marathon Petroleum above all, plus gas producers, refiners and fuel distributors.
money: pipelines, terminals, marine transport and fuels distribution
gathering, processing and fractionating natural gas and liquids
moat: Pipeline corridors and processing plants that cannot be rebuilt, with capacity contracted under long-term minimum-volume agreements.
risks: Debt of about $27 billion is large relative to earnings
Marathon Petroleum controls it, so minority holders have limited influence
Gathering volumes depend on drilling activity
It is a partnership, which complicates taxes for some investors
opportunities: A distribution yield above 8% is covered by contracted cash flow
Natural gas liquids demand from petrochemicals and exports keeps growing
Expansion projects in the Permian basin add contracted capacity
watch: Distributable cash flow coverage of the distribution and new project commitments.
